title: The sub-$4 headline that still costs you more

lines: The average gallon of gas just dropped below $4 for the first time since July.
Feels like a win at the pump.
Here's the part the headline skips.
You're paying about 23% more to fill up than last Thanksgiving.
Flying costs more too — AAA members are paying about $800 round-trip, up 17% from a year ago.
So for the first time since 2008, AAA expects fewer people to travel:
A sub-$4 sign is nice, but the bill that matters is the one against last year — and that one went up.
Driving, flying, or staying home this Thanksgiving?

source_line: Source: AAA — gas average & Thanksgiving forecast, Nov. 17, 2026
caption:
Gas just dropped below $4 for the first time since July — and somehow Thanksgiving still got pricier.

The national average is $3.78 a gallon (AAA, today), down from $4.31 a month ago. But a year ago it was $3.07 — so you're paying about 23% more to fill up than last November. Airfare's up too: AAA members are paying around $800 round-trip, 17% more than last year.

For the first time since 2008 — outside the pandemic — AAA expects fewer Thanksgiving travelers: 81.5 million, a hair under last year.

My take: a sub-$4 pump price makes a great headline, but the bill against last year still went up.
